checks.name: typecheck passes
lint passes
unit tests pass
production build succeeds
pi-web HEAD and its six pre-existing user changes are untouched
no credential or key material is present in the shipped tree
no screenshot, native binary or archive is committed
the credential files that must never be committed are absent
checks.detail: auth.json and .env must not exist in the repository

checks.name: the release ignore rules exclude dependencies and build output
no build output or dependency directory is staged for release
the license inventory records every installed production dependency
no AGPL, GPL-3 or SSPL component is present
every installed production dependency declares a license
the MPL-2.0 components are named with their source location
checks.detail: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md must name the MPL components and how to obtain their source

checks.name: the project ships its own license text
checks.detail: package.json declares MIT, so a LICENSE file must exist

checks.name: the changelog records the current version as unreleased or released
the support matrix records the project version
the support matrix records the locked desktop driver version
checks.detail: the driver version must appear in the supported-version record

checks.name: the support matrix distinguishes verified from unverified combinations
checks.detail: a matrix that lists only verified rows would hide the gaps

checks.name: the desktop driver is pinned to the locked version in package.json
Electron is pinned to the version the native checks used
the Pi SDK is pinned to the version the pi-web baseline uses
every native acceptance record exists
the native acceptance records keep their unverified items
the .gitignore excludes local agent goal state while keeping project .pi configuration versionable
checks.detail: ignoring all of .pi would make future project configuration unversionable

checks.name: the README states the status truthfully
checks.detail: a release README must not present unverified capability as working

summary.note: this gate checks what can be automated; the manual steps for the unverified capability are recorded in the corresponding evidence README files
